newsitem.title: USA: Goldman Sachs sees Indonesian rupiah fairly valued.
newsitem.headline: Goldman Sachs sees Indonesian rupiah fairly valued.

text.p: Despite concerns over political stability and President Suharto's health, the Indonesian currency has adhered to its fair value, Goldman Sachs said in its "Weekly Analyst" on Tuesday.
According to the Goldman Sachs model, a long-run equilibirum value for the rupiah is 2,395 per U.S. dollar for the average of August 1996, compared to the aveage spot rate of 2,332 per dollar.
The Indonesian economy in 1995 grew faster than any year since 1991, to which the government responded with tigher macroeconomic polcies to prevent overheating.
Slower exports would lead to marginally wider current account deficits about 3.9 percent of the GDP in 1996 before retreating in 1997.
"We do not see a change in Indonesia's policy of steady depreciation of the rupiah at 4.5 - 5.0 percent, which is considered consistent with a steady real exchange rate," it says.

Despite politcal uncertinty economic fundamentals are improving with slowing inflation and a manageable trade imbalance. The central bank will therefore attempt to keep interest rates up in coming months to slow the economy,
"We believe limited pressure on the currency due to political fall-out is likely to be met with higher intrest rates rather than devaluation," it says
The rupiah is forecast to be at 2,354, 2,372, 2,400 and 2,456 per dollar at one-, three-, six- and 12-month horizeon, in line with the corresponding forwards.
